}}'''Antoine Danchin''' (born 7 May 1944) is a French [[geneticist]]. He is best known for his research in several fields of biology, from the structure and function of [[adenylate cyclase]], to modelling of learning in the nervous system and the early development of [[genomics]] and [[bioinformatics]]. He is the chairman of the startup AMAbiotics which specialises in metabolic bioremediation and synthetic biology. He was the director of the Department Genomes and Genetics at the [[Pasteur Institute]] in Paris where he headed the Genetics of Bacterial Genomes Unit.

== Early life and career ==
He was trained as a mathematician at the [[Institut Henri Poincaré]] and a physicist at the [[École Normale Supérieure]]. Working first with [[Mildred Cohn]], [[Marianne Grunberg-Manago]] and Ionel Solomon in [[nuclear magnetic resonance]], Danchin became an experimental [[microbiologist]] in the early seventies.
He created with [[Philippe Courrège]] and [[Jean-Pierre Changeux]] at the [[Institut de biologie physico-chimique]] in Paris, France, a working seminar where they worked together on the construction of mathematical models of learning and memory.<ref name="Changeux1973">{{cite journal |last1=Changeux |first1=J.-P. |last2=Courrege |first2=P. |last3=Danchin |first3=A. |title=A Theory of the Epigenesis of Neuronal Networks by Selective Stabilization of Synapses |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |date=1973-10-01 |volume=70 |issue=10 |pages=2974–2978 |doi=10.1073/pnas.70.10.2974|pmid=4517949 |pmc=427150 |bibcode=1973PNAS...70.2974C |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Interested in University training he created, with [[Maurice Guéron]], the first semester of Biology at the [[École polytechnique]], and developed his teaching during four years. Among his first students one can find Daniel Kahn, [[Patrick Charnay]], and many others. The main goal of his research has been to try to understand how genes can function collectively in the cell. This led him to work on regulation systems which control global gene expression in bacteria. Part of his work was devoted to the study of the enzymes that synthesize cyclic AMP. He established the reference classification of adenylate cyclases<ref name="Danchin1993">{{cite journal |last1=Danchin |first1=A |title=Phylogeny of adenylyl cyclases. |journal=Advances in Second Messenger and Phosphoprotein Research |date=1993 |volume=27 |pages=109–62 |pmid=8418825}}</ref> after his laboratory successfully cloned and sequenced the genes of adenylyl cyclase [[toxins]] from the [[whooping cough]] agent<ref name="Glaser1988">{{cite journal |last1=Glaser |first1=P |last2=Ladant |first2=D |last3=Sezer |first3=O |last4=Pichot |first4=F |last5=Ullmann |first5=A |last6=Danchin |first6=A |title=The calmodulin-sensitive adenylate cyclase of Bordetella pertussis: cloning and expression in Escherichia coli. |journal=Molecular Microbiology |date=January 1988 |volume=2 |issue=1 |pages=19–30 |doi=10.1111/j.1365-2958.1988.tb00003.x |pmid=2897067|s2cid=205365386 }}</ref> as well as from the agent of [[anthrax]].<ref name="Escuyer1988">{{cite journal |last1=Escuyer |first1=Vincent |last2=Duflot |first2=Edith |last3=Sezer |first3=Odile |last4=Danchin |first4=Antoine |last5=Mock |first5=Michèle |title=Structural homology between virulence-associated bacterial adenylate cyclases |journal=Gene |date=November 1988 |volume=71 |issue=2 |pages=293–298 |doi=10.1016/0378-1119(88)90045-5|pmid=2906312 }}</ref> This work led him to trigger ethical reflections on the practices of molecular genetics and genomics at a time when this was not considered important.<ref name="Danchin2002">{{cite journal |last1=Danchin |first1=Antoine |title=Not every truth is good: The dangers of publishing knowledge about potential bioweapons |journal=EMBO Reports |date=February 2002 |volume=3 |issue=2 |pages=102–104 |doi=10.1093/embo-reports/kvf040|pmid=11839688 |pmc=1083978 }}</ref>

Danchin started in 1985 a collaboration with computer scientists for evaluation of [[artificial intelligence]] techniques to the study of integrated problems in [[molecular genetics]].<ref name="Gascuel1986">{{cite journal |last1=Gascuel |first1=Olivier |last2=Danchin |first2=Antoine |title=Protein export in prokaryotes and eukaryotes: Indications of a difference in the mechanism of exportation |journal=Journal of Molecular Evolution |date=December 1986 |volume=24 |issue=1–2 |pages=130–142 |doi=10.1007/BF02099961|pmid=3104613 |bibcode=1986JMolE..24..130G |s2cid=931622 }}</ref> This convinced him that it was time to investigate genomes as wholes, provided that an important effort in computer sciences was initiated in parallel ([[in silico]] biology). Early in 1987 he proposed that a sequencing program should be undertaken for ''[[Bacillus subtilis]]''. This proposal was actualized by a European joint effort on this genome, starting in 1988. This led him to try to organize [[bioinformatics]] in France with the help of several colleagues at universities, [[CNRS]] and [[INRIA]], through the creation of a nationwide group, GDR 1029 (1991–1995) and subsequently through the coordination of the bioinformatics programme of the Groupement de Recherche et d'Etudes des Genomes (1992–1996), then at the Comité de Coordination des Sciences du Vivant (1998–2000). Re-sequencing and re-annotation of the ''B. subtilis'' genome was completed in 2009 to update the sequence and annotation of this [[reference genome]].<ref name="Barbe2009">{{cite journal |last1=Barbe |first1=Valérie |last2=Cruveiller |first2=Stéphane |last3=Kunst |first3=Frank |last4=Lenoble |first4=Patricia |last5=Meurice |first5=Guillaume |last6=Sekowska |first6=Agnieszka |last7=Vallenet |first7=David |last8=Wang |first8=Tingzhang |last9=Moszer |first9=Ivan |last10=Médigue |first10=Claudine |last11=Danchin |first11=Antoine |title=From a consortium sequence to a unified sequence: the Bacillus subtilis 168 reference genome a decade later |journal=Microbiology |date=2009-06-01 |volume=155 |issue=6 |pages=1758–1775 |doi=10.1099/mic.0.027839-0|doi-access=free |pmid=19383706 |pmc=2885750 }}</ref>

In year 2000, Danchin created the HKU-Pasteur Research Centre in Hong Kong, meant to develop microbial genomics in the region, with the help of the Innovation and Technology Commission of the Hong Kong SAR government to develop bioinformatics (programme Biosupport).<ref name="biosupport">{{cite web |title=Welcome to the Biosupport web page |url=http://bioinfo.hku.hk/ |access-date=28 May 2021 |date=2009-09-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090919112405/http://bioinfo.hku.hk/ |archive-date=19 September 2009 }}</ref>

Danchin is now developing theoretical reflections and experiments in the domain of [[synthetic biology]],<ref name="de Lorenzo2008">{{cite journal |last1=de Lorenzo |first1=Víctor |last2=Danchin |first2=Antoine |title=Synthetic biology: discovering new worlds and new words: The new and not so new aspects of this emerging research field |journal=EMBO Reports |date=September 2008 |volume=9 |issue=9 |pages=822–827 |doi=10.1038/embor.2008.159|pmid=18724274 |pmc=2529360 }}</ref> trying to make explicit the idea that cells behave as computers ([[Turing machines]]) making computers.<ref name="Danchin2009">{{cite journal |last1=Danchin |first1=Antoine |title=Bacteria as computers making computers |journal=FEMS Microbiology Reviews |date=January 2009 |volume=33 |issue=1 |pages=3–26 |doi=10.1111/j.1574-6976.2008.00137.x|pmid=19016882 |pmc=2704931 }}</ref> Together with [[Victor de Lorenzo]], he created the free and open access journal ''Symplectic Biology'', devoted to publishing innovative ideas in systems and synthetic biology.<ref name="symplectic_biol">{{cite web |title=symplectic biology: rapid research notes in systems and synthetic biology |url=http://www.normalesup.org/~adanchin/bibliography/flyer_SymB.pdf}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Antoine Danchin is the father of [[Raphael Danchin]].
